Add entity

  
Opened from a text selection, so the name has already been through the documented title case conversion and the Context row still holds the phrase it came from. Edit the name and watch the IRI, the duplicate check and the planned source follow. Type Enginee in Parents to see the resource picker, and type a name that does not exist to draft a parent inside the same transaction.


  
The title case rules, implemented

  
docs/text-analysis.md specifies this precisely, so it is code here rather than prose. The menu has a Re-run the title case conversion item and the three published examples are in it.

  

    
SelectionNameRule

    
      
Basic ENGLISH COMPOSITIONBasic English CompositionAll uppercase words are capitalised

      
PHD SEMINAR IN GISPhD Seminar in GISListed acronyms take their canonical spelling, and a small word inside the title goes lowercase

      
iPhone accessoryiPhone AccessoryMixed case is left alone, so iPhone and McGraw survive

      
the theory of flightThe Theory of FlightAll lowercase words are capitalised; of stays down because it is neither first nor last

    
  

  
The conversion runs only when a selection first opens this view. Names you type, and parent names you type, keep your spelling, which is why editing the field does not re-title-case it as you go.


  
Nested parent drafts and one transaction

  
docs/find-similarity.md is explicit: "New parents and the class are committed together in one undoable transaction" and "Source there includes the complete planned hierarchy." Type an unknown parent name and the picker offers to draft it; the chip is dashed, the nested row takes its own parent, and the planned source grows to include it. Create writes the whole set as one operation, and one Undo removes all of it.


  
What the name check actually checks

  
Three separate things, reported separately rather than as one red field: whether the name is already used by a class in the store, whether the IRI that this name would occupy is taken by anything at all, and whether the characters need percent encoding to be a legal IRI. A name collision offers to reveal the existing class, because the documented behaviour of opening a duplicate is to show you its actual page rather than to refuse.


  
The planned source is the first thing to go

  
It is a second column above 860 pixels wide and 400 tall, and it is absent everywhere else. Not folded under the form, not reduced to a sliver: gone. The form plus the commit action is the irreducible content of this view, and the preview is the one region that can leave without taking a fact with it, because the form already states everything the source serialises.

  
860 is the published threshold for carrying a second region alongside a primary editor, and the arithmetic underneath it is what makes the withdrawal right rather than merely tidy. The longest line this preview emits is about 62 monospace characters, roughly 470 pixels. A fixed 320 pixel column clips that line at every pane width, so at an 800 pixel pane the preview was taking 40 percent of the view, leaving the form 480, and still scrolling horizontally. It cost the form real width and bought an unreadable preview. Above 860 the column takes 34 percent instead of a fixed 320, so it stops being a sliver exactly where there is width to spend on it, and the form never drops below about 540.

  
Nothing becomes unreachable. Copy the planned source stays in the overflow menu at every size, including recovery, so the full serialisation is one action away whether or not the column is on screen. The draft, the parents, the nested drafts and the validation survive every one of these transitions.


  
What is seeded rather than read from your store

  
The existing class list the picker and the duplicate check search, the occupied IRI set, and the text selection this draft opened from. The title case conversion, the picker, the nested drafts, the three name checks and the escaped source are all real.
